proposals.impact: restores automated content pipeline, unblocks queue growth
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 06:54 UTC and the Funnel-Hack Digest failed at 11:33 UTC. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published. Both automated pipelines are down on the same day. If the blog workflow stays broken, the queue empties inside 24 hours and organic SEO traffic loses its daily feed — which is upstream of every quiz, email, and booking conversion in the funnel.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and read the most recent failure log. The commit history shows active development on the booking page and cash-flow model branch (PR #54), so a dependency version conflict or a changed environment variable is the most probable cause. Fix the root error in the workflow YAML or the script it calls, confirm the Funnel-Hack Digest shares no broken dependency, and re-run both. Do not touch .github/workflows/* production files without reading the failure output first — the safety rules block those paths for good reason, so this is a Joel-must-act item, not a Fred-can-auto-ship item.
proposals.new_text:
# ACTION REQUIRED — Joel to run manually
# 1. Go to Actions tab > Daily Blog Post > most recent failed run > expand the failing step.
# 2. Copy the error message.
# 3. Check whether the same env var or package is referenced in Funnel-Hack Digest.
# 4. Apply the fix, re-run both workflows, confirm green.
# Estimated time: 20 minutes. Cost of inaction: queue hits zero before tomorrow's window.

proposals.impact: removes the single point where all quiz traffic currently stops
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, one session hit the quiz at intro_load and stopped. Zero starts, zero completions, completion rate 0%. The sole source is the deploy-preview URL for PR #54, not the production domain, which means this is a preview-environment visitor (likely a developer or Joel himself) rather than a cold prospect. Even so, the intro screen is the only place where every future visitor will make the go/no-go decision. If the CTA copy or button on that screen is thin, the production version will bleed the same way when real traffic arrives.
proposals.proposal: Audit the QuizIntro component's headline and primary CTA button text. The current pattern on many quiz tools is a generic "Start the quiz" button under a vague promise headline — that combination fails the Sultanic test instantly. Replace both with copy that names the specific tension Joel's ICP feels at 11 pm on a Sunday when they earn well but the savings account hasn't moved in eight months. Ground it in the £150k-earner-who-still-feels-broke reality, not a generic curiosity hook.
proposals.new_text:
Find out why your income keeps rising and your savings account keeps not

See your money script in 4 minutes

proposals.impact: lifts open rate from 37.5% toward the 66% Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance automation: 12 sent, 8 opens, 66.67% open rate. Money Worship automation: 16 sent, 6 opens, 37.5% open rate. That is a 29-percentage-point gap on a larger send volume. The Vigilance sequence is clearly doing something right in its subject line or sender name preview. The Worship sequence is reaching more people and converting fewer of them to opens — which means the problem is almost certainly in the subject line, not the content, because they never got past it.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of the first email in the Money Worship automation. The working hypothesis is that the current subject line either sounds like a compliment ("You value money!" reads as flattering, so the reader feels no tension to resolve) or it is too abstract. Pull the subject line from the Vigilance email that is landing at 66% and study its structure — then write a Worship-specific subject line that names the quiet cost of the Worship script rather than describing it. Something that makes a 28-year-old who bought a watch they couldn't afford feel a small, honest jolt of recognition, not shame.
proposals.current_text: subject: Your money personality result: Money Worship
proposals.new_text: subject: The watch (or the holiday, or the course) felt like progress. Was it?
